evidence: Ruined Air player.gd implements aerodynamic glide physics using mass, wing area, air density, angle-of-attack lift, stall clamp, induced drag, dynamic pressure, lift/drag forces, boost heat/overheat, 3D steering and speed cap.

Ruined Air world generator builds separated floating island centers, inverted-cone noisy rock masses, graph bridges, small rocks, an MST plus extra edges, and a density field consumed by voxel chunks.
Ruined Air voxel chunks polygonize the world density field with Marching Cubes, density-gradient normals and generated trimesh collision.
Ruined Air player scene uses Scavenger_new.fbx, a head-bone camera, foot IK targets and PlayerBoneHandler.gd; it also includes a physical spiked glider model and glide icon.
Arcane Manifold already uses a full-body Forgeborn rig with head-bone camera, PlayerBoneHandler, external foot IK and SkeletonIK3D, supporting Drew's body-presence transmission claim.

Drew identifies Ruined Air as the successor to the unnamed asteroid game whose rooms were placed inside a sphere; Ruined Air carried forward Arcane Manifold body presence, turned the spatial idea into floating rocks, and became an ancestor of modern Infinite Brutality.
Recording shows first-person embodied view beneath a deployed glider moving through large floating rock masses and open-air traversal geometry.
